concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: A way of comparing growth rates of functions, ignoring constant factors.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of powers of a variable with coefficients, multiplied and reduced in the usual way.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a and b and imaginary unit i, with i² = −1.

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine that reads and writes symbols on one or more tapes, each with a movable head.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape machine model
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, whose size does not grow with the input.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Exact integer multiplication
concepts.gloss: Given binary strings x and y of length n, output the 2n-bit binary representation of their product.

evidence.quote: We consider exact multiplication

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth of the time needed to multiply two n-bit integers.

evidence.quote: proposed n log n as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.gloss: The known fixed-tape integer multiplier running in O(n log n) time, used here only as a black-box subroutine.

evidence.quote: Calls to the established O(n log n)

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing both integers as polynomials in a power of two whose coefficients are their digits, so that their product is a polynomial convolution of short coefficients.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map sending a vector of q values to its q values weighted by powers of a q-th root of unity, normalized by 1/q.

evidence.quote: We now implement the normalized Fourier transforms needed for convolution

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two sequences in which indices wrap around modulo the sequence length.

evidence.quote: denote cyclic convolution in the displayed axes

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: A technique that replaces a Fourier transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map
concepts.gloss: A relabeling of coefficient positions by mixed-radix digits for pairwise coprime lengths, which turns one cyclic convolution into a multidimensional cyclic convolution.

evidence.quote: a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: An identity that rewrites a Fourier transform as a cyclic convolution multiplied by chirp factors, so that it can be computed with convolution.

evidence.quote: Bluestein’s chirp identity converts the middle transform

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Fourier-type transforms whose roots of unity are powers of y in a polynomial ring, so that multiplying by a root is a signed shift of coefficients.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomial ring, whose powers act as roots of unity.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of polynomials with complex coefficients in which y^r is identified with −1, so that y has order 2r and wrap-around flips a sign.

evidence.quote: the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo y r + 1

concepts.name: Phase twist
concepts.gloss: A coefficientwise multiplication by roots of unity that converts the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial ring, so its wrap-around becomes the negative wrap of that ring.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing
concepts.gloss: Encoding polynomial coefficients, including negative ones, as one large integer by fixed-width blocks, so that polynomial multiplication becomes integer multiplication.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: The normalized product of two arrays of records in the polynomial ring, computed by two forward synthetic transforms, a pointwise product, and an opposite transform.

evidence.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order

concepts.name: Subspace labels
concepts.gloss: Nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space attached to each wire of a network, whose inclusions control how much work a change of representation costs.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear

concepts.name: Linear networks and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values while restoring scratch values, in which each vertex carries an invertible operator called its frame.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values

concepts.name: Subset-intersection network
concepts.gloss: A linear network on the three-element subsets of a ground set, whose wires carry scalars and whose gates combine them by intersection size, so that it swaps two banks while cancelling arbitrary scratch values.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients

concepts.name: Address-field interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that swaps two disjoint contiguous address fields of an array in time that grows like a power of the field width, rather than linearly.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in an array

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The map that updates two address fields H, D to H + D, D, which is implemented by a small number of field interchanges.

evidence.quote: that endpoint operator is an address shear

concepts.name: Rank-saving recursion
concepts.gloss: The recursion in which each call splits into s smaller calls on streams of 1/W of the volume, where s < W m, so that the cost grows by the strictly smaller factor s/W per level.

evidence.quote: the total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < W m

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadics
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are integers divided by a power of two, with the Gaussian integer part also an integer.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Complex phase network
concepts.gloss: A subset-intersection network whose frame change on each edge is a product of two-point kernels aI + bX on Gaussian dyadic values.

evidence.quote: The complex phase network of Proposition 8

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of the two-point map H0 applied to several selected address bits at once, computed exactly in one pass rather than one axis at a time.

evidence.quote: a common butterfly layer on several axes

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: An operation that adds one selected bit position across several address chunks at once, using cyclic shifts and a small deterministic correction for exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle

concepts.name: Guard-width bound
concepts.gloss: An explicit number of extra fractional and integer bits that makes every intermediate coefficient of a butterfly layer exact, so that a single final truncation suffices.

evidence.quote: An explicit guard-width bound

concepts.name: Transform layout
concepts.gloss: A permutation of address bits that places the selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive chunks, so that a simultaneous butterfly layer applies to each transform round.

evidence.quote: A layout on which the parallel layers apply

concepts.name: Prime source lengths
concepts.gloss: Distinct odd primes chosen close to the powers of two that are the padded axis lengths, so that their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths si must be close to the powers of two ti

concepts.name: Transform identity with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: The Gaussian resampling identity in which the source and target coordinate permutations are kept as part of the formula, so that they cancel across a convolution instead of being executed as sorts.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula

concepts.name: Carry propagation
concepts.gloss: Converting the recovered integer radix-digit coefficients into a binary string by adding each coefficient to a carry from the previous position.

evidence.quote: Propagate radix-2b carries in increasing coefficient order

concepts.name: Exact coefficient recovery
concepts.gloss: The error analysis showing that the computed convolution coefficients are within a half of their true integer values, so rounding recovers them exactly.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below 1/2

concepts.name: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape machine that multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time with κ = 2^−182, which disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine A

concepts.name: Big-Theta, big-Omega and little-o notation
concepts.gloss: Θ(f) and Ω(f) bound a function from above and below up to constant factors, and o(f) denotes growth strictly smaller than f.

concepts.name: Logarithms
concepts.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the power to which the base b must be raised to give x, and log2 x measures bit lengths.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: For a real x, the floor is the largest integer at most x and the ceiling is the smallest integer at least x.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all integers by checking a base case and showing that each case implies the next.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations
concepts.gloss: An equation or inequality that defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms, solved by unrolling it into a closed form.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.gloss: The sum of a^j for j from 0 to k, which equals (a^(k+1) - 1)/(a - 1) when a is not 1.

concepts.name: Sets, intersections and indicator vectors
concepts.gloss: The intersection of two finite sets is the set of elements they share, and the indicator vector of a set is the 0/1 vector that marks its elements.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijection from a finite set to itself, and it reorders the entries of a list or array.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: An order on tuples that compares first entries first, then second entries, and so on.

concepts.name: Positional (radix) notation
concepts.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, and mixed-radix notation lets each position have its own base.

concepts.name: Hamming weight
concepts.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary string is the number of its entries equal to 1.

concepts.name: Two's complement and signed binary
concepts.gloss: A signed n-bit integer is stored in two's complement, where the leading bit has weight minus 2^(n-1), and sign extension pads it to a wider width.

concepts.name: Fixed-point binary numbers
concepts.gloss: A fixed-point number has a fixed number of bits after the binary point, so that sums and products are exact when enough extra bits are kept.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Two integers are congruent modulo n when their difference is a multiple of n, and arithmetic is carried out on residue classes.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
concepts.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer factors uniquely into primes.

concepts.name: Binary field GF(2) and XOR
concepts.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is exclusive-or and multiplication is AND.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: A complex number z is an n-th root of unity when z^n = 1, and it is primitive when no smaller positive power of it equals 1.

concepts.name: Polar form and Euler's formula
concepts.gloss: Every complex number can be written as r e^(i theta) = r(cos theta + i sin theta), with modulus r and argument theta, and its conjugate reverses the sign of the imaginary part.

concepts.name: Vector spaces over a field
concepts.gloss: A vector space over a field is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, and a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space.

concepts.name: Matrices, rank and invertibility
concepts.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map, its rank is the dimension of its column space, and it is invertible exactly when its rank equals its size.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Gaussian elimination applies elementary row operations to reduce a matrix to echelon form, and triangular matrices are those with zero entries on one side of the diagonal.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
concepts.gloss: An eigenvalue of a square matrix is a scalar lambda for which some nonzero vector v satisfies Av = lambda v.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: An iterative method that improves an approximate root x of f by replacing it with x - f(x)/f'(x).

concepts.name: Stable sorting and radix sort
concepts.gloss: A stable sort keeps equal keys in their original order, and radix sort sorts by keys digit by digit using stable passes from least to most significant digit.

cyclic-convolution.name: cyclic convolution
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two vectors of equal length, whose indices wrap around modulo the length.
cyclic-convolution.quote: The cyclic convolution of $u$ and $v$, written $u\ast v$, has entries

cyclic-convolution.name: entry index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: An index of a vector entry, an element of $\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: For vectors $u$ and $v$ of length $s$, index the entries by $i,j,m \in \mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$, that is, by $0,\dots,s-1$ with sums taken modulo $s$.

cyclic-convolution.name: entry index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: A second index of a vector entry, an element of $\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: For vectors $u$ and $v$ of length $s$, index the entries by $i,j,m \in \mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$, that is, by $0,\dots,s-1$ with sums taken modulo $s$.

cyclic-convolution.name: output index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The index of an entry of the cyclic convolution, an element of $\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: For vectors $u$ and $v$ of length $s$, index the entries by $i,j,m \in \mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$, that is, by $0,\dots,s-1$ with sums taken modulo $s$.

cyclic-convolution.name: entry count
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The number of entries of an array indexed by the axes $s_1,\dots,s_d$, namely $s_1 s_2\cdots s_d$.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $S=s_1s_2\cdots s_d$, the number of entries of such an array (so $S=s$ when $d=1$).

cyclic-convolution.name: retained source permutation
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The coordinate permutation of the source vectors that is kept in the formula and cancels across the convolution.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Write $R$ for the retained source permutation, the $P_s$ of the resampling identity, with inverse $R^{-1}$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: vector length
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The number of entries in the input and output vectors, a count.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $q$ be the number of entries in the vector.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: primitive root of unity
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A primitive q-th root of unity, whose powers weight the sum.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $\omega$ be a primitive $q$-th root of unity, so $\omega^q = 1$ and the powers $\omega^0, \omega^1, \dots, \omega^{q-1}$ are distinct.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input vector
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The list of q complex input entries that the transform acts on.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{q-1})$ be the input vector, where $a_j$ is the entry at position $j$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: transformed vector
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The list of q output entries, the transform of a.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Its transform $\hat a = (\hat a_0, \dots, \hat a_{q-1})$ has $q$ entries, where $\hat a_k$ is the output at position $k$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input position index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an input entry, running from 0 to q-1.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $j$ and $k$ be indices running from $0$ to $q-1$, where $j$ runs over input positions and $k$ over output positions.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: output position index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an output entry, running from 0 to q-1.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $j$ and $k$ be indices running from $0$ to $q-1$, where $j$ runs over input positions and $k$ over output positions.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: first input
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: A binary string of length n, the first of the two inputs.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be binary strings of length $n$, the two inputs.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: second input
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: A binary string of length n, the second of the two inputs.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be binary strings of length $n$, the two inputs.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: input bit count
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The number of bits in each input string.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Here $n$ is the number of bits in each input.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: value function
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The function mapping a binary string to its nonnegative integer value, with the leftmost bit most significant.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: For a binary string $x$, $\mathrm{val}(x)$ is its nonnegative integer value, with the leftmost bit most significant.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: padded bit width
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The number of bits of the padded binary representation.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Here $k$ is the number of bits of the padded representation and $z$ is an integer with $0 \le z < 2^k$.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: integer to encode
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: An integer with 0 at most z and z less than 2 to the power k, which is encoded by bin_k.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Here $k$ is the number of bits of the padded representation and $z$ is an integer with $0 \le z < 2^k$.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: padded binary representation
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The function giving the binary representation of an integer z, padded on the left with zeros to exactly k bits.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Then $\mathrm{bin}_k(z)$ is the binary representation of $z$ padded on the left with zeros to exactly $k$ bits.

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of a source vector, a count.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of a target vector, a count.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian width
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The integer $\alpha$ is the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.

gaussian-resampling.name: source transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length s, sending g to the vector with entries g_{ti}.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_i=g_{ti}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $i$ is the source coordinate index, $0\le i<s$, and $m$ is the target coordinate index, $0\le m<t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length t, sending h to the vector with entries h_{-sm}.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_i=g_{ti}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $i$ is the source coordinate index, $0\le i<s$, and $m$ is the target coordinate index, $0\le m<t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source coordinate index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The index of a coordinate of a source vector, running over 0 to s-1.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_i=g_{ti}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $i$ is the source coordinate index, $0\le i<s$, and $m$ is the target coordinate index, $0\le m<t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target coordinate index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The index of a coordinate of a target vector, running over 0 to t-1.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_i=g_{ti}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $i$ is the source coordinate index, $0\le i<s$, and $m$ is the target coordinate index, $0\le m<t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: identity map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $I$ is the identity map.

gaussian-resampling.name: operator norm
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The operator norm, the largest factor by which a linear map stretches a vector.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm, the largest factor by which a linear map stretches a vector, where the size of a vector is its largest absolute coordinate.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian map S
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian map T
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: diagonal Gaussian map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The diagonal map on vectors of length s that multiplies coordinate i by a Gaussian factor.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $i$ by a Gaussian factor.

gaussian-resampling.name: selection map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map taking a vector of length t to the coordinates at the indices nearest ti/s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $C$ selects from a vector of length $t$ the coordinates at the indices nearest $ti/s$, for $0\le i<s$; for $s=3$ and $t=4$ it picks indices $0$, $1$ and $3$, nearest to $0$, $4/3$ and $8/3$.

gaussian-resampling.name: near-identity map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map CTD from vectors of length s to themselves, close to the identity.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Put $N=CTD$, a map close to $I$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The contraction S/2 applied to vectors of length s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Fourth, the maps $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$ are the two contractions of the identity.

gaussian-resampling.name: target contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The contraction 2^{-(2 alpha^2-2)} D N^{-1} C/2 from vectors of length t to vectors of length s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Fourth, the maps $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$ are the two contractions of the identity.

gaussian-resampling.name: summation index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series, the exponent of I-N in each term.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Its inverse is $N^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge 0}(I-N)^r$, where $r$ is the summation index, the exponent of $I-N$ in each term.

radix-digit-convolution.name: radix
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The base of the digit expansion, an integer at least 2.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Fix a radix $B \ge 2$, the base in which the inputs are written.

radix-digit-convolution.name: first input
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two integers to multiply, and let $d$ be the number of radix-$B$ digits of each input, so $x=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}x_iB^i$ and $y=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}y_jB^j$, where $x_i$ and $y_j$ are the digits.

radix-digit-convolution.name: second input
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two integers to multiply, and let $d$ be the number of radix-$B$ digits of each input, so $x=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}x_iB^i$ and $y=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}y_jB^j$, where $x_i$ and $y_j$ are the digits.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit count
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of radix-B digits of each input, a count.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two integers to multiply, and let $d$ be the number of radix-$B$ digits of each input, so $x=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}x_iB^i$ and $y=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}y_jB^j$, where $x_i$ and $y_j$ are the digits.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit of x
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The i-th radix-B digit of x, counting from the least significant digit.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two integers to multiply, and let $d$ be the number of radix-$B$ digits of each input, so $x=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}x_iB^i$ and $y=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}y_jB^j$, where $x_i$ and $y_j$ are the digits.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit of y
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The j-th radix-B digit of y, counting from the least significant digit.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two integers to multiply, and let $d$ be the number of radix-$B$ digits of each input, so $x=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}x_iB^i$ and $y=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}y_jB^j$, where $x_i$ and $y_j$ are the digits.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit vector of x
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The vector (x_0, ..., x_{d-1}) of the digits of x.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $u=(x_0,\dots,x_{d-1})$ and $v=(y_0,\dots,y_{d-1})$ be the digit vectors.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit vector of y
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The vector (y_0, ..., y_{d-1}) of the digits of y.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $u=(x_0,\dots,x_{d-1})$ and $v=(y_0,\dots,y_{d-1})$ be the digit vectors.

radix-digit-convolution.name: convolution of digit vectors
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The convolution of u and v, whose m-th entry is the sum of u_i v_j over i+j=m.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The inner sum, written $(u\ast v)_m$, is the convolution of $u$ and $v$ at index $m$.

transform-identity.name: source box array
transform-identity.meaning: An array indexed by the source box, one of the two inputs to the convolution.
transform-identity.quote: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be arrays indexed by the source box, which has $M=\prod_i s_i$ entries, where $s_i$ is the length of source axis $i$.

transform-identity.name: second source box array

transform-identity.quote: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be arrays indexed by the source box, which has $M=\prod_i s_i$ entries, where $s_i$ is the length of source axis $i$.

transform-identity.name: source box size
transform-identity.meaning: The number of entries of the source box, the product of the source axis lengths.
transform-identity.quote: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be arrays indexed by the source box, which has $M=\prod_i s_i$ entries, where $s_i$ is the length of source axis $i$.

transform-identity.name: opposite transform
transform-identity.meaning: The source transform with the sign of its roots of unity reversed.
transform-identity.quote: Let $F_s^{+}$ be the opposite transform, whose roots of unity have reversed sign.

gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling is a technique that replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

Gaussian resampling is applied to a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md): it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for that convolution by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

radix-digit-convolution.quote: Radix-digit convolution rewrites an integer product as a polynomial product: it reduces [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to a convolution of short digit vectors.

transform-identity.quote: The transform identity rests on [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
The transform identity cancels its retained permutation across a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md).

exact-integer-multiplication: Exact integer multiplication is the problem of multiplying two binary integers and returning every bit of the product, with no rounding or truncation.
The target result is a faster algorithm for this problem, so this page fixes its exact input and output.
The width $2n$ suffices because each value is at most $2^n-1$, so the product is at most $(2^n-1)^2<2^{2n}$.
Harvey and van der Hoeven later reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper bound (cited).
The target result improves the $O(n\log n)$ bound (cited).

background.summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree, so they know big-O and related asymptotic notation, polynomials, complex numbers (roots of unity, polar form), and Turing machines with tapes. They also know the discrete mathematics and first linear algebra that every such degree teaches: modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, sets, permutations, binary and radix notation, XOR over GF(2), induction, recurrences and geometric sums, and vector spaces, matrices and Gaussian elimination over a field, with basic sorting. They have not met the Chinese remainder theorem, the FFT, tensor products, bilinear forms, Gaussian integers, prime-number estimates, or operator norms and Neumann series.
